radar_checked: 2026-11-07T08:10+08:00 MetMalaysia composite radar (COMP_SS): cells offshore west of Kudat and over northern Sarawak; nothing over Kota Kinabalu at that time.

sections.label: TODAY
sections.text: A fine, hot morning: the airport reported only a few low clouds overnight and at 08:00, while the blended model drew near-total cloud at the same hours, so expect more sun than the model suggests this morning. The 08:10 radar showed no rain near Kota Kinabalu. Afternoon thunderstorms are favoured: the KK airport forecast (TAF) has temporary thunderstorm rain during 14:00–18:00 MYT; MetMalaysia's town forecast says thunderstorms this afternoon and rain tonight (the district forecast adds 'in a few places'); the blended model's hourly rain chance climbs through late morning (55% at 11:00, 72% at 12:00, 88% at 13:00), so showers could start before the TAF period. Today's model highs run 28.7–33.1°C (median 31.5°C); MetMalaysia gives 32°C for the town and 33°C for the district, and the airport measured 33°C yesterday. I favour 32–33°C.

sections.label: RAIN AMOUNT
sections.text: The ECMWF ensemble's 10th–90th percentile for the airport grid point today is 2.0–10.5 mm, with a 12% chance of 10 mm or more. That is a grid-point daily total, not a storm-specific figure: a spot under a cell can get far more, and a spot a few km away can stay dry.

sections.label: THIS WEEK
sections.text: Dry mornings and afternoon thunderstorms are the pattern all week. Two different signals point to more disruption later in the week: the ensemble's chance of a 10 mm+ day rises from 12% today to 29% on Tuesday and 37% on Wednesday, then eases to 25% and 22%; MetMalaysia's district wording broadens from thunderstorms in a few places (Sat–Tue) to most places (Wed) and widespread (Thu–Fri), while the town record says thunderstorms each afternoon without a coverage word. So Wednesday carries the highest rain-total risk and Thursday–Friday the widest official storm coverage. Highs 32–33°C, lows 24–25°C. Separately, MetMalaysia has a continuous-rain alert for Kudat and the Sandakan areas (9–11 Nov) and strong north-east winds around Reef North offshore (8–10 Nov); neither names Kota Kinabalu.

sections.label: PLAN
sections.text: Put outdoor work, site visits and long drives in the early morning and reassess before midday. Carry an umbrella from late morning. Western Sabah coastal waters were under a thunderstorm warning until 09:00 today, dangerous to small boats; check the latest bulletin before going out to sea.

sections.label: CONFIDENCE
sections.text: Temperature: moderate (official forecast and yesterday's measurement agree; models are spread). Timing of this afternoon's storms: moderate (TAF, MetMalaysia and the model peak agree on the afternoon, but exact local timing stays uncertain). Rain amount at your exact spot: low.

sections.label: WHY
sections.text: Forecasts issued 24 hours ahead were checked against yesterday's airport readings: hourly temperature errors ran from 1.0°C (GFS) to 2.9°C (ARPEGE), with ECMWF and the blend about 0.5–0.8°C too cool on average and ICON, GEM and CMA 1.4–2.1°C too warm; all but ARPEGE predicted rain in the 14:00–18:00 window, and the airport reported an active thunderstorm 14:15–16:30 with light rain and recent-thunderstorm remarks at 16:42 and 17:00. One day proves nothing about persistent bias; the comparison panel keeps running daily. Possible reasons for the spread, not established: coastal grid boxes mixing land and sea, and the Crocker Range behind the city.
